name: Familial Patent Arterial Duct

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Patent Arterial Duct

criteria.description: Echocardiographic evidence of persistent patency of the arterial duct beyond 3 months of age
Positive family history of patent arterial duct or congenital heart defects
Presence of continuous 'machinery' murmur on cardiac auscultation
Signs of congestive heart failure or exercise intolerance in infancy or early childhood

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Echocardiographic confirmation of patent arterial duct plus positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging and family history; clinical signs support but are not definitive.

searchTerms: continuous heart noise heard with stethoscope

pathognomonic.symptomName: Echocardiographic visualization of patent ductus arteriosus
searchTerms: heart ultrasound showing open ductus arteriosus
imaging of persistent fetal heart vessel

common.symptomName: Tachypnea due to increased pulmonary blood flow
searchTerms: rapid breathing from increased lung blood flow
fast breathing due to pulmonary overload
tachypnea caused by excess pulmonary circulation
failure to gain weight as baby
large difference between systolic and diastolic blood pressure
shortness of breath with activity in older kids

occasional.symptomName: Left ventricular enlargement on physical exam
searchTerms: enlarged left heart chamber felt on exam
big left heart on clinical exam

occasional.symptomName: Mild cyanosis in cases with pulmonary hypertension
searchTerms: slight bluish skin tint from lung pressure
mild cyanosis due to pulmonary hypertension
high lung blood pressure with reversed shunt
pulmonary hypertension causing blood flow reversal
infection of heart near ductus arteriosus

rare.symptomName: Arrhythmias secondary to cardiac chamber enlargement
searchTerms: abnormal heart rhythm secondary to chamber size

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible elevated BNP in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography showing persistent ductus arteriosus with left-to-right shunting
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular markings
genetic: Familial inheritance pattern suggesting autosomal dominant transmission in some families
other: Cardiac catheterization may be used to assess pulmonary pressures and shunt size

distinguishingFeatures: Similar clinical presentation but no inherited pattern

redFlags: Signs of congestive heart failure in infancy
Recurrent respiratory infections with failure to thrive
references: Orphanet: Familial Patent Arterial Duct - ORPHA:466729
